recall_prompt: Say the multiplication theorem, then say how it is proved from the two conditional probability definitions.
insider_note: The statement needs both conditions P(A) ≠ 0 and P(B) ≠ 0 — each one is what allows one of the two divisions in the proof.

steps.label: State the theorem
steps.margin_note: First mark. Name the events, state both non-zero conditions, and write both forms of the product.

lines.text: Statement: If A, B are two events of a random
experiment with P(A) ≠ 0 and P(B) ≠ 0, then

recall.must_convey: That for events A, B with P(A) ≠ 0, P(B) ≠ 0, P(A ∩ B) = P(A)·P(B|A) = P(B)·P(A|B).
accept: if P A and P B are non zero then P of A intersection B equals P A times P B given A equals P B times P A given B
the intersection is P A into P B given A and also P B into P A given B
multiplication theorem P A and B equals P A P B given A
P A, P B non zero ayithe P of A intersection B ante P A into P B given A, P B into P A given B

steps.why: The theorem gives the probability of "both" for events that need not be independent; the conditional probability carries the dependence.
common_mistakes: Writing P(A ∩ B) = P(A)·P(B), which is only the independent case.

steps.label: From the definition of P(B|A)
steps.margin_note: Second mark. P(B|A) = P(A ∩ B)/P(A), allowed because P(A) ≠ 0; multiply across.

lines.text: Proof: By the definition of conditional probability,

recall.must_convey: That P(B|A) = P(A ∩ B)/P(A) by definition, so P(A ∩ B) = P(A)·P(B|A).
accept: by definition P B given A is P A intersection B over P A so the intersection is P A times P B given A
cross multiply the definition of B given A
the conditional probability definition gives equation one
P B given A definition nunchi P A intersection B ante P A into P B given A

steps.why: The definition of conditional probability is the only thing the proof uses; the theorem is the definition rearranged.
common_mistakes: Writing the definition as P(B|A) = P(A ∩ B)/P(B).

steps.label: From the definition of P(A|B)
steps.margin_note: Third mark. The same definition with the roles swapped, allowed because P(B) ≠ 0.

lines.text: Again, by the definition of conditional probability,

recall.must_convey: That P(A|B) = P(A ∩ B)/P(B) by definition, so P(A ∩ B) = P(B)·P(A|B).
accept: similarly P A given B is P A intersection B over P B so the intersection is P B times P A given B
swap the roles and cross multiply again
the second definition gives equation two
P A given B definition nunchi P A intersection B ante P B into P A given B

steps.why: The second form of the theorem needs the second conditional probability; P(B) ≠ 0 is what permits this division.
common_mistakes: Skipping this step and writing the second form without proof.

steps.label: Combine (1) and (2)
steps.margin_note: Last mark. Both equal P(A ∩ B), so they equal each other.

recall.must_convey: That equations (1) and (2) together give P(A ∩ B) = P(A)·P(B|A) = P(B)·P(A|B).
accept: from one and two the intersection equals both products hence proved
combine the two equations to get the theorem
both expressions equal P A intersection B so they are equal
one and two nunchi P A intersection B ante rendu products, hence proved

steps.why: Two expressions for the same probability are equal to each other; that equality is the statement.
common_mistakes: Ending at (2) without writing the combined line.
